source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 874 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 874 was established by Ordinance No. 28830, passed by the Dallas City Council on October 24, 2012. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 874 is established on property located on the south side of Bandera Avenue, between Turtle Creek Boulevard and Hillcrest Road. The size of PD 874 is approximately 2.521 acres. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this district:

(1) BLADE SIGN means a sign projecting perpendicularly from a main building facade, visible from both sides, and made of rigid or soft materials.

(2) STOOP means a small porch leading to the entrance of a residence.

(3) TANDEM PARKING means one parking space in front of another parking space, making it necessary to pass through one parking space to gain vehicular access to the other parking space.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 874A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 874A). Lots 1, 2, and 3 are shown on the conceptual plan. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Except as provided in this section, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) A development plan is not required to obtain a building permit for a temporary leasing office. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

(1) Residential uses.

-- Multifamily. -- Retirement housing.

(2) Utility and public service uses.

-- Local utilities. -- Tower/antenna for cellular communication. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator.

(c) The following accessory uses are permitted by SUP only:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Amateur communication tower. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MF-3(A) Multifamily District apply.

(b) Setbacks for residential uses.

(1) In general.

(A) A temporary leasing office may be located in a required setback.

(B) In Lot 3, no portion of a window that faces west may be located within 21 feet of the western Property line.

(2) Lot 1.

(A) Minimum setback from the western perimeter of Lot 1 is 30 feet, measured from the centerline of the Northwest Plaza Drive access easement, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(B) Minimum setback from the northern Property line is 20 feet, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(C) Minimum setback from the eastern Property line is five feet, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(3) Lots 2 and 3.

(A) Minimum setback from the eastern perimeter of Lots 2 and 3 is 20 feet, measured from the centerline of the Northwest Plaza Drive access easement, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(B) Minimum setback from the northern Property line on Lot 2 is 20 feet, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(C) Minimum setback from the western Property line on Lot 2 is five feet, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(D) Minimum setback from the western Property line on Lot 3 is 17 feet, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(E) Minimum setback from the southern Property line on Lot 3 is 10 feet, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(4) Projections.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph and Section 51P-874.113(b)(3), balconies, bay windows, awnings, patios, signs, and entryways affixed to a building or part of the foundation may project up to five feet into the required setback.

(B) In Lot 3, balconies are prohibited within 21 feet of the western Property line.

(C) Stoops, retaining walls, benches, pots, raised planters, sculptures, and other decorative landscaping may be located within or project into a required setback, but may not be located within or project into an easement.

(5) Urban form setback. No urban form setback is required.

(c) Density. For multifamily uses, maximum number of dwelling units is 198.

(d) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 78 feet.

(2) Mechanical equipment located on top of a building may project a maximum of 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(e) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 75 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Residential uses.

(1) One off-street parking space for each bedroom is required, with a minimum of one off-street parking space per dwelling unit.

(2) If the off-street parking provided for each dwelling unit is restricted to resident parking only, one-quarter of an off-street parking space per dwelling unit is required for guest parking.

(3) Off-street parking is not required for accessory uses.

(4) Tandem parking is permitted for resident parking only.

(c) Existing parking. Existing angled parking spaces shown on the conceptual plan along Bandera Avenue may be counted toward the total combined parking requirements for the Property. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) One small tree must be provided every 25 feet on center along the perimeter of the western Property line of Lot 3.

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.113. SIGNS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Blade signs. The following regulations apply to multifamily uses:

(1) A maximum of two blade signs are permitted.

(2) Maximum effective area for a blade sign is 72 square feet.

(3) A blade sign may project up to four feet into a required setback.

(4) Blade signs may not be internally illuminated.

(5) Blade signs are prohibited on building facades facing Bandera Avenue. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Facade Materials
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.114. FACADE MATERIALS.

To ensure compatibility with surrounding uses, building facades must be at least 70 percent masonry, excluding windows, entrances, and ingress and egress points. Masonry includes stone, brick, concrete, hollow clay tile, cementitious fiber siding, decorative concrete blocks or tile, glass blocks, other similar materials, or a combination of these materials. For purposes of this provision, stucco is considered masonry but Exterior Finish Insulations System (EFIS) materials are not. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Except as provided in this subsection, a temporary leasing office may operate on the Property for up to 180 days from the date the building permit is issued. If construction of the residential uses has not been completed, the building official may grant additional 30-day extensions for the temporary leasing office.

(b) A minimum three-foot-wide sidewalk or walking path must be provided along the entire northern perimeter of Lot 2 adjacent to Bandera Avenue. The sidewalk or walking path materials may be permeable or nonpermeable.

(c) For purposes of complying with Section 51A-4.601(a)(1) or other provisions requiring that lots front upon a dedicated public or private street, the existing access and utility easements shown on the conceptual plan are considered dedicated public or private streets.

(d) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(e) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 28830)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-874.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 28830)
